A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 36 pages of each version, including Appendices A–C, are readable and support a reliable text and visual comparison.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports mathematical inequalities, sharpness constructions, and theoretical estimation guarantees. It contains no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the theoretical scope, including its empirical Bayes application. No original empirical results appear in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: The Gaussian-mixture model, Yatracos estimator in (53), regularized Bayes estimator, and tuning choices are unchanged. Appendix C revises their mathematical justification, not their procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or performs empirical task evaluations. The Gaussian-mixture and Huber-contamination settings remain theoretical models with unchanged coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. The discussions of NPMLE and other estimators are unchanged.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols are present in either version. The retained theoretical sampling model and estimator-tuning prescriptions are unchanged.

E4.justification: The sharpness constructions and supplementary mathematical analyses are retained. Neither version contains empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness tests, or error analyses.

E5.justification: The theoretical concentration bounds are unchanged. Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Neither PDF reports empirical result entries. The final theoretical rates and sharpness conclusions remain unchanged; the numerical corrections concern intermediate proof inequalities assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 corrects the TV approximation error from 4ε to 4η and changes (54) to bound TV(P,P̂), replacing TV(fπ,f̂). Appendix C.2 adds the contamination triangle-inequality step in (57), changing 3ε to 4ε, and propagates this correction into Theorem 4.5's proof. Theorem 4.7's proof also explicitly invokes a discretization argument. The theorem statements and asymptotic rates are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about sharp TV–Hellinger inequalities, resolution of the prior open problem, and applications to minimax estimation and empirical Bayes.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including compact support, fixed isotropic covariance, computational inefficiency of the Yatracos estimator, and unresolved optimal sample-size dependence.

D1.justification: Estimator definitions and tuning prescriptions are retained. Moving the definition of f̂ within Appendix C adds no implementation information, and neither version supplies code, data-access instructions, or computational experiment details.

R1.justification: Appendix C.2 replaces the local generalization remark citing Jiang and Zhang (2009) with an explicit attribution to the discretization argument in Saha and Guntuboyina (2020), Theorem 3.5. This is a limited revision to proof attribution; the bibliography and overall research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Small edits in Appendix C standardize covering-radius notation, relocate the density-estimator definition, and refine proof explanations. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while the main text and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix C has limited changes to equation width, line wrapping, and spacing, particularly around the expanded inequality (57). The overall layout and Section 3 construction diagram remain unchanged; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Appendix C distinguishes the covering radius from contamination, explicitly accounts for the additional contamination error, and updates downstream constants consistently. It also clarifies the proof dependency for Theorem 4.7. These limited corrections improve rigor and traceability; the slightly looser intermediate constants leave the methods and final rates unchanged.
